title: 2003 AMC 12B Problem 23
statement: The number of \(x\)-intercepts on the graph of \(y = \sin(\frac{1}{x})\) in the interval \((0.0001, 0.001)\) is closest to

solutions.text:
The intercepts occur where \(\frac{1}{x} = k\pi,\) that is \(x = \dfrac{1}{k\pi}\) for a nonzero integer \(k.\)

The condition \(0.0001 \lt \dfrac{1}{k\pi} \lt 0.001\) becomes \[ \frac{1000}{\pi} \lt k \lt \frac{10000}{\pi}. \]

The number of such integers is \[ \begin{aligned} &\left\lfloor \frac{10000}{\pi} \right\rfloor - \left\lfloor \frac{1000}{\pi} \right\rfloor \\ &= 3183 - 318 = 2865, \end{aligned} \] closest to \(2900.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: \(\sin(\frac{1}{x}) = 0\) when \(\frac{1}{x} = k\pi\) for a nonzero integer \(k,\) i.e. \(x = \dfrac{1}{k\pi}\)
